before: <para id="fs-id1171242343847">As electromagnetic waves are received, as described above, the forces exerted on the charged particles (see <link document="m58496" target-id="fs-id1171242369180"/> for diagrams) do work on the particles and increase its energy. The energy that sunlight carries is a familiar part of every warm sunny day. A much less familiar feature of electromagnetic radiation is the extremely weak pressure that electromagnetic radiation produces by exerting a force in the direction of the wave. This force occurs because electromagnetic waves contain and transport momentum.</para>
